prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1028; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim received by phone from the insured driver. Rear-end collision at a signalized intersection, insured vehicle struck from behind by a sedan. Claimant reports neck pain and stiffness starting shortly after the impact. No police report filed at scene; exchanged information with the other driver. Opened bodily injury and property damage files.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant by phone. Claimant reports whiplash-type symptoms: neck stiffness, headache, limited rotation to the left. Claimant states she was seen at an urgent care clinic the same day and given a cervical collar and prescription for muscle relaxants. Claimant is not represented by an attorney and says she does not currently plan to retain one. Explained the claims process and requested medical records authorization.

Entry 3: Received signed medical authorization from claimant. Requested records from urgent care clinic and primary care provider covering the prior three years to establish any preexisting neck complaints. Photos of the vehicle damage received from claimant's submission. Rear bumper and trunk lid damage consistent with reported impact. Reviewing repair estimate.

Entry 4: Claimant called to ask about the status of the injury claim and whether a settlement offer would be made soon. Explained that the file is pending receipt of treatment records and that no offer can be made until the medical picture is complete. Claimant reports physical therapy has begun, two sessions per week, and that she is still experiencing morning stiffness. Advised claimant of her right to seek legal advice at any time, and to contact the department if she has questions about the handling of her claim.

Entry 5: Urgent care and primary care records received and reviewed. Records show no prior cervical complaints in the period reviewed and are consistent with the account of injury. Repair estimate approved for the property damage. Requested updated treatment notes from physical therapy provider. Scheduled a follow-up call with claimant in two weeks to check on recovery progress and any additional expenses.
